proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_periodic_neg_one_black_times (p N : ℕ)
    (hc : ∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn (t + p) = centerColumn t)
    (t : ℕ) (ht : N ≤ t) (hb : centerColumn t = true) :
    evolve (t + p) (-1) = evolve t (-1) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE BLACK TIMES OF A PERIODIC CENTRE COLUMN PIN COLUMN -1, SO THE RESIDUAL OF P1 IS THE WHITE TIMES AND NOTHING ELSE. Why it is true: at a black centre cell the rule at the origin loses its middle input, so the next centre cell is the complement of the cell one to the left (centerColumn_succ_of_black). Read that at t and at t + p: a p-periodic centre column makes the two left-hand cells complements of the same bit, so they are equal. WHY AN OPEN NODE WOULD CITE IT: centerColumn_periodic_damage_white (open, size L, no route) becomes twelve lines with this in hand, and I have compiled that proof (explorer/seeder_scratch_p1d.lean, axioms propext and Quot.sound). The argument: suppose past some M every white time repeated column -1 too; this lemma covers the black times; so column -1 is p-periodic from max M N, column 0 is p-periodic from N, and not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent at i = -1 forbids two adjacent eventually periodic columns. The same lemma is the black-time half of centerColumn_not_isEventuallyPeriodic_of_white_times in this tier. Recommended for seeding by the theorist attack of 2026-09-08 ('the residual itself', C3: 'with the black times pinned by column_succ_of_black, the wall is a statement about column 1 at the white times of the centre column and about nothing else'); it was never seeded.
proposals.disclaims: Does not prove P1 and does not weaken either wall. Its hypothesis is the negation of P1, so nobody can exhibit a p and N satisfying it and it carries NO WITNESS: a finite range would only confirm the hypothesis is unsatisfiable there, which is not what is claimed. It says nothing whatever about the white times, which is the entire open part. It is also not a settling or agreement-front statement and does not run into obstruction 69: it never reads a fixed bit of the packed row.

route.tactics:
have hbp : centerColumn (t + p) = true := by rw [hc t ht, hb]
have a := centerColumn_succ_of_black t hb
have b := centerColumn_succ_of_black (t + p) hbp
have e : centerColumn (t + p + 1) = centerColumn (t + 1) := by
  rw [show t + p + 1 = t + 1 + p by ring]; exact hc (t + 1) (by omega)
rw [a, b] at e
exact Bool.not_inj e

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_not_isEventuallyPeriodic_of_white_times
    (h : ∀ p > 0, ∀ N : ℕ, (∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn (t + p) = centerColumn t) →
        ∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn t = false → evolve (t + p) 1 = evolve t 1) :
    ¬ IsEventuallyPeriodic centerColumn := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: A SUFFICIENT CONDITION FOR PRIZE 1, IN THE SHAPE THE WALL ASKS FOR: to prove that the centre column never repeats it is enough to control column 1 at the WHITE times of a hypothetically periodic centre column. Everything else is already pinned. Why it is true: split the times past the onset by the colour of the centre cell. At a black time, column -1 repeats for free (centerColumn_succ_of_black at t and t + p, the black-times lemma of this tier). At a white time, column_one_of_white says column 1 is the xor of the next centre cell with column -1, so the hypothesis plus the centre column's own period makes column -1 repeat there too. Column -1 is then eventually periodic and so is column 0, which not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent at i = -1 forbids. WHY A PROOF OF THE WALL WOULD CITE IT: it is the model centerColumn_other_of_cohomologous_column in a second coordinate, and it converts the wall from a statement about an existential over all columns into a statement about ONE named column at a NAMED SUBSET of times. PROVED IN SCRATCH: explorer/seeder_scratch_p1c.lean, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. By column_one_of_white the hypothesis is interchangeable with the same statement about column -1 at white times, which is exactly the negation of the open node centerColumn_periodic_damage_white; the two are one object seen from either side of the origin.
proposals.disclaims: IT IS NOT THE WALL AND IT DOES NOT WEAKEN IT. What it buys is a smaller target, not an easier one: nothing here says the residual (column 1 at the white times) is any more tractable than P1, and I claim no evidence that it is. The hypothesis is a conditional whose antecedent is the negation of P1, so it is unsatisfiable in fact, no p and N can be exhibited, and the node carries NO WITNESS by design rather than by omission. Anyone who proves the hypothesis has proved Prize 1, which is the point and also the warning.

route.tactics:
rintro ⟨p, hp, N, hN⟩
have h1 := h p hp N hN
refine not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent (-1) ⟨⟨p, hp, N, ?_⟩, ⟨p, hp, N, ?_⟩⟩
· intro n hn
  show evolve (n + p) (-1) = evolve n (-1)
  have e : centerColumn (n + p + 1) = centerColumn (n + 1) := by
    rw [show n + p + 1 = n + 1 + p by ring]; exact hN (n + 1) (by omega)
  cases hc : centerColumn n with
  | true =>
      have hcp : centerColumn (n + p) = true := by rw [hN n hn, hc]
      have a := centerColumn_succ_of_black n hc
      have b := centerColumn_succ_of_black (n + p) hcp
      rw [a, b] at e
      exact (Bool.not_inj e)
  | false =>
      have hcp : centerColumn (n + p) = false := by rw [hN n hn, hc]
      have a : evolve n 1 = xor (centerColumn (n + 1)) (evolve n (-1)) :=
        column_one_of_white initialConfig n hc
      have b : evolve (n + p) 1 = xor (centerColumn (n + p + 1)) (evolve (n + p) (-1)) :=
        column_one_of_white initialConfig (n + p) hcp
      rw [e, h1 n hn hc, a] at b
      revert b
      cases centerColumn (n + 1) <;> cases evolve n (-1) <;> cases evolve (n + p) (-1) <;> simp
· intro n hn
  show evolve (n + p) ((-1 : ℤ) + 1) = evolve n ((-1 : ℤ) + 1)
  rw [show (-1 : ℤ) + 1 = 0 by ring]
  exact hN n hn

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_black_infinitely_often (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ t ≥ N, centerColumn t = true := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: HALF OF THE PERIOD-1 CASE OF PRIZE 1, AND IT IS PROVABLE: the centre column is never white for good. Why it is true: at a white centre cell the rule at position 1 loses its xor term and becomes an OR, so column 1 at the next step is column 1 or column 2 at this one. If the centre column were white from N on, column 1 could therefore never turn from black back to white after N, so it is monotone, so it is eventually constant, so it is eventually periodic — and so is the centre column, with period 1. Two adjacent columns cannot both be eventually periodic (not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent at i = 0). WHY AN OPEN NODE WOULD CITE IT: centerColumn_not_eventually_constant (open, size L) is LITERALLY the conjunction of this node and centerColumn_white_infinitely_often, in that order — it closes as one anonymous constructor once both land. PROVED IN SCRATCH with a self-contained route needing no other node of this tier: explorer/seeder_scratch_p1e.lean, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
proposals.disclaims: Nothing above period 1. There is no induction on the period here and none is available: this half turns on a monotonicity that exists only when the centre column is white at EVERY late time, and one black cell in a period destroys it. So it is not a step toward either P1 wall, and the tier does not pretend it is. A mathematician would call this easy and would very likely call it folklore; it is not in any source held here, but I did not search the literature and it should not be reported as novel. The witness is a genuine instance check rather than a shadow — every N below 8 really does get a black cell below 12 — but it says nothing about large N, where the whole claim lives.

route.tactics:
by_contra hcon
push_neg at hcon
have hN : ∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn t = false := by
  intro t ht
  have := hcon t ht
  cases hx : centerColumn t with
  | false => rfl
  | true => exact absurd hx this
have mono : ∀ t, N ≤ t → evolve t 1 = true → evolve (t + 1) 1 = true := by
  intro t ht hb
  have e : evolve (t + 1) 1 = (evolve t 1 || evolve t 2) := by
    rw [evolve_succ, rule30_eq]
    norm_num
    rw [show evolve t 0 = false from hN t ht]
    simp
  rw [e, hb]; rfl
have key : ∃ M, N ≤ M ∧ ∀ n ≥ M, evolve (n + 1) 1 = evolve n 1 := by
  by_cases hex : ∃ t, N ≤ t ∧ evolve t 1 = true
  · obtain ⟨t0, ht0, hb⟩ := hex
    refine ⟨t0, ht0, ?_⟩
    have all : ∀ s, evolve (t0 + s) 1 = true := by
      intro s
      induction s with
      | zero => simpa using hb
      | succ k ih =>
          have := mono (t0 + k) (by omega) ih
          rw [show t0 + (k + 1) = t0 + k + 1 by ring]
          exact this
    intro n hn
    have e1 : evolve (n + 1) 1 = true := by
      rw [show n + 1 = t0 + (n + 1 - t0) by omega]; exact all _
    have e2 : evolve n 1 = true := by
      rw [show n = t0 + (n - t0) by omega]; exact all _
    rw [e1, e2]
  · push_neg at hex
    refine ⟨N, le_refl _, ?_⟩
    intro n hn
    have e1 : evolve (n + 1) 1 = false := Bool.not_eq_true _ |>.mp (hex (n + 1) (by omega))
    have e2 : evolve n 1 = false := Bool.not_eq_true _ |>.mp (hex n (by omega))
    rw [e1, e2]
obtain ⟨M, hNM, hcol1⟩ := key
refine not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent 0 ⟨⟨1, one_pos, M, ?_⟩, ⟨1, one_pos, M, ?_⟩⟩
· intro n hn
  show centerColumn (n + 1) = centerColumn n
  rw [hN (n + 1) (by omega), hN n (by omega)]
· intro n hn
  show evolve (n + 1) ((0 : ℤ) + 1) = evolve n ((0 : ℤ) + 1)
  rw [show (0 : ℤ) + 1 = 1 by ring]
  exact hcol1 n hn

witness.expression: (List.range 8).all (fun N => (List.range 12).any (fun t => decide (N ≤ t) && centerColumn t))

proposals.statement:
theorem centerColumn_white_infinitely_often (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ t ≥ N, centerColumn t = false := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: THE OTHER HALF OF THE PERIOD-1 CASE OF PRIZE 1: the centre column is never black for good. Why it is true: at a black centre cell the next centre cell is the complement of the cell one to the left (centerColumn_succ_of_black). If the centre column were black from N on, that reads as 'true equals not L', so column -1 is white at every time from N on — eventually periodic with period 1 — while the centre column is black at every time from N on, also eventually periodic. Adjacent columns cannot both be eventually periodic (not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent at i = -1). WHY AN OPEN NODE WOULD CITE IT: with centerColumn_black_infinitely_often it is exactly centerColumn_not_eventually_constant (open, size L), whose statement is the conjunction of the two in the other order. PROVED IN SCRATCH: explorer/seeder_scratch_p1c.lean, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
proposals.disclaims: Nothing above period 1, and no induction on the period is implied or available — this half and the black half use completely different mechanisms (one the left neighbour, one a monotonicity on the right), which is why neither generalises and why the pair is not a step toward either P1 wall. Almost certainly folklore in mathematical terms; not found in the sources held here, but not searched for either, so it should not be reported as novel. The witness is a real instance check for N < 8, not a shadow, and it is silent about every N above 7.

route.tactics:
by_contra hcon
push_neg at hcon
have hN : ∀ t ≥ N, centerColumn t = true := by
  intro t ht
  have := hcon t ht
  cases hx : centerColumn t with
  | true => rfl
  | false => exact absurd hx this
refine not_isEventuallyPeriodic_adjacent (-1) ⟨⟨1, one_pos, N, ?_⟩, ⟨1, one_pos, N, ?_⟩⟩
· intro n hn
  show evolve (n + 1) (-1) = evolve n (-1)
  have h1 : ∀ m, N ≤ m → evolve m (-1) = false := by
    intro m hm
    have hb := centerColumn_succ_of_black m (hN m hm)
    rw [hN (m + 1) (by omega)] at hb
    cases hx : evolve m (-1) with
    | false => rfl
    | true => rw [hx] at hb; simp at hb
  rw [h1 (n + 1) (by omega), h1 n (by omega)]
· intro n hn
  show evolve (n + 1) ((-1 : ℤ) + 1) = evolve n ((-1 : ℤ) + 1)
  rw [show (-1 : ℤ) + 1 = 0 by ring]
  show centerColumn (n + 1) = centerColumn n
  rw [hN (n + 1) (by omega), hN n hn]

proposals.statement:
theorem column_one_succ_of_white (X : Config) (t : ℕ) (h : column X 0 t = false) :
    column X 1 (t + 1) = (column X 1 t || column X 2 t) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: COLUMN 1 CAN ONLY LOSE ITS BLACK AT A BLACK CENTRE CELL. Why it is true: the rule at position 1 is 'cell 0 xor (cell 1 or cell 2)', and a white cell 0 deletes the xor, leaving the OR. So at every white centre time column 1 moves upward and never downward. WHY THE TIER NEEDS IT: it is the mechanism of centerColumn_black_infinitely_often, and it is the forward-in-time companion of the two laws the board already has at the origin — column_succ_of_black (black centre, sideways) and column_one_of_white (white centre, sideways). Those two say what a white or black centre cell does to the column on its LEFT; this is the first that says what a white centre cell does to the column on its RIGHT, which is the column the residual of centerColumn_not_isEventuallyPeriodic_of_white_times is about. Stated over an arbitrary configuration, like its two companions, so a half-line or damage argument can use it. PROVED IN SCRATCH: explorer/seeder_scratch_p1.lean, axioms propext and Quot.sound.
proposals.disclaims: Unconditional and true of every configuration, so by itself it rules nothing out — it is one unfolding of rule30_eq and a mathematician would call it a definition chase, not a result. It gives monotonicity only across a white centre cell; at a black one column 1 becomes the complement of the same OR and the monotonicity is gone, which is exactly why the period-1 argument it feeds does not reach period 2. WITNESS NON-VACUITY CHECKED: the hypothesis holds at t = 2, 6, 7 in range over the seed, and the same expression with column 3 in place of column 2 evaluates to false, so the check can fail.
